text:
releasebot: DeployBot: hotfix candidate v2026.03.23-llm-router-patch queued for prod-llm-router (region: us-central1). Trigger: surge of 502s from router -> model-hosts starting ~15:12Z. Spike affects realtime chat. CI: green. Please ack and provide expedited approval or rollback criteria. Link: https://redwood-internal/release/2026.03.23-llm-router-patch

ji: tagging SRE + infra oncall. quick Q: does this change request/response headers or model API?

liam: short: small fix in router proxy that truncates long X-User-Meta header under heavy parallelism (commit d4e5f6). No model code changes.

maya: customer-facing errors, starting to get pager alerts. we should fasttrack canary. propose "traffic-preserve" canary: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. health windows: 1m, 3m, 7m, manual hold at 25%. rollback triggers: 502 rate > baseline + 0.4% OR total customer error count increase > 15 in 5m OR new alert from oncall.

cory: infra OK with fasttrack if 2 approvers sign. need release note snippet and container image tags. rollback image: registry/redwood/llm-router:v2026.03.22-stable.

liam: i can approve. image built: registry/redwood/llm-router:v2026.03.23-rlfix. sha: sha256:abcdef123456. changelog PR: https://redwood-internal/pr/2319

cory: +1 from ops. approving expedited canary. :white_check_mark:

releasebot: Approvals received: liam, cory. Initiating canary: pin 1% traffic to v2026.03.23-rlfix. Canary plan: 1m -> 5m -> 25m hold manual.

releasebot: Deploy command executed by liam: ```
kubectl set image deployment/llm-router router=registry/redwood/llm-router:v2026.03.23-rlfix --record
kubectl rollout status deployment/llm-router -n prod --watch
# traffic-shift (load-balancer): redwood-lb set-weight prod-llm-router v2026.03.23-rlfix 1
```

ji: watching logs and upstream connection errors. posting quick snapshots: routing-502 ~30 -> 4 after initial pod spin up.

releasebot: Canary 1% done -> healthchecks pass -> promoted to 5% (window 3m).

maya: metrics look better at 5%. p50/p95 stable. customer error count dropped. holding until 25%.

ji: no increase in latency. no new alerts.

releasebot: manual bump requested by liam -> moving to 25% canary hold.

cory: monitoring dashboards OK. continuing watch. if we see any regressed downstream services, we rollback.

liam: if rollback needed: run: ```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/llm-router -n prod
redwood-lb set-weight prod-llm-router v2026.03.23-rlfix 0
redwood-lb set-weight prod-llm-router v2026.03.22-stable 100
```

releasebot: 25% held for 7m, metrics within thresholds. proceeding to 100% per expedited flow.

maya: rolling to 100% now. will keep oncall loop active for 30m.

releasebot: Rollout complete. All routers on v2026.03.23-rlfix. Release notes published: https://redwood-internal/docs/releases/2026-03-23-llm-router-patch

ji: will draft a short blameless postmortem about header sizing and add an automated alert for header-truncation errors.

cory: ops action: add a unit test for header edge cases and a runbook entry for fast rollback commands.

maya: thanks all. if any oddities surface ping this thread and execute rollback commands above. :raised_hands:
